title: Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
summary: A rope extension with the arms overhead, so the triceps long head works from a deep stretch. The app's go-to triceps isolation move: triceps 1, long head 1.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: cable station with an adjustable pulley.

muscles.why: All three heads straighten the elbow. The long head also crosses the shoulder, and with the arm overhead it is stretched across both joints, so the library rates it 1 and the short (lateral and medial) heads 0.7.

region_notes.text: Overhead cable extensions grew the triceps, the long head most of all, clearly more than pushdowns in a 12-week study.

setup.text: Set the pulley at about hip to chest height and attach a rope.
Turn away from the stack, rope behind your head, and step forward into a staggered stance until the weight lifts.
Lean forward slightly with your abs braced, elbows pointing forward beside your head.

form_cues.why: Elbows that point forward keep the upper arm overhead, which is what stretches the long head.
Only the forearms move; the elbow is the hinge.
The long-head stretch at the bottom is the reason to choose this exercise.

form_cues.cue: Get a deep stretch at the bottom of every rep.
form_cues.why: Same idea as the cue: the deep bottom position is where this lift does its best work.
Stops the lower back arching so the arms, not the torso, move the rope.

bias_tweaks.change: Keep the upper arm close to your ears rather than in front of your face
bias_tweaks.effect: More shoulder flexion, so the long head is longer through the whole rep.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Go only as far overhead as your shoulders allow comfortably.

bias_tweaks.change: Add bottom-half (lengthened) partials when full reps run out
bias_tweaks.effect: Extends the set in the stretched part of the range; lengthened partials matched full reps for elbow-extensor growth in trained people.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Full reps work as well; partials are an option, not a requirement.

bias_tweaks.change: One arm at a time with a single handle
bias_tweaks.effect: Lets you match reps between arms and find a comfortable path for each elbow.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Same wording as the swap tag 'One side at a time'.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Letting the elbows flare out to the sides.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows about shoulder width and pointing forward; lighten the load if they drift out.

mistakes.text: Bending the torso forward and back to move the rope.
mistakes.fix: Brace in a fixed lean; only the forearms move.

mistakes.text: Stopping well short of the stretch.
mistakes.fix: Let the rope travel behind your head until the triceps are long.

mistakes.text: Turning it into a pullover by moving the upper arms.
mistakes.fix: Fix the upper arms overhead; if they move, the weight is too heavy.

misconceptions.myth: Pushdowns and overhead extensions grow the triceps the same.
misconceptions.reality: With the same sets, overhead extensions grew the triceps more, especially the long head.
Light and heavy loads gave similar growth when sets were taken close to failure. Heavy loads build more strength.

lower_risk.text: The app adds no ramp-up sets here. If the muscle is not warm from earlier work, make the first set a little lighter.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 2 reps in reserve in the 10-15 rep range. End the set when the elbows start to flare or the torso starts to help.
Lower into the stretch under control; don't let the rope yank your arms back.
If the overhead position doesn't feel right for your shoulders, lower the elbows a little or use a skull crusher, which keeps the arm less overhead.

alternatives.why: Arms at your sides, so the short heads lead (short heads 1, long head 0.6).
Free-weight extension with the arm partly overhead; still a good long-head stretch (long head 0.9).
Hardest at lockout instead of in the stretch; a preference, no growth advantage shown.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: No equipment; the triceps still help (rating 0.6) alongside the chest.

notes: The long-head growth result comes from one 12-week study comparing overhead extensions with pushdowns.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
